task_reconstruction.official_task: 2023 MCM Problem C, as restated on page 3.
required_outputs: prediction interval for number of reported outcomes on March 1, 2023
analyze word attribute effect on hard mode selection
predict distribution of reported outcomes for EERIE
classify solution words by difficulty, classify EERIE
describe other interesting features of dataset

section_map.summary: abstract: summary sheet with TASK 1-4 structure
introduction: pages 3-5, Homer anecdote + lit review + paper structure
data-preprocessing: page 6, word length + outlier correction
model-establishment: pages 6-14, Gaussian + Poisson + relaxation + mode analysis
problem-analysis: pages 14-17, BP NN + Bagging + uncertainty
results: pages 17-21, K-Means + Pearson + EERIR classification

contributions.summary: Trend-fluctuation decomposition with Gaussian regression + Poisson process.
Popularity relaxation function correcting Poisson intensity by game heat.
Three lifecycle periods (Explosion, Fading, Dormant) by analogy with public opinion.
Bagging-integrated BP NN with hard voting for distribution prediction.

dependency_graph.label: BP NN predicted distribution feeds K-Means difficulty classification.

assumptions.summary: Reported users reflect actual player changes.
One play per person per day, reset at 0:00 EST.
Players have literacy and problem-solving skills.
Historical data represents all possible questions.

data_and_preprocessing.summary: Word length anomalies (4 or 6 letters) corrected from answer data.
No.529 outlier corrected by 2-day moving average.

models.summary: BP NN + Bagging: 7-h-7, K=20, correlation 0.84, EERIE (0,1,6,25,31,25,13)%.
K-Means + Pearson: 4 levels, VN=0.90, WCN=0.82, EERIR=Master.

verification.summary: Gaussian regression R2=0.9988, RMSE 2 orders smaller than data.
Pearson r: F2=0.81, WCN=0.82, VN=0.90 > threshold 0.6.

results_trace.summary: Word attributes do not affect hard mode selection (scatter analysis).
Hard mode percentage increases over time, then levels off.

writing_logic.summary: Homer anecdote connects Cambridge Dictionary to Wordle popularity.
Data exploration decomposes time series before modeling.
Public opinion lifecycle analogy justifies three periods.
Mechanistic modeling dismissed for data-driven BP NN.
Difficulty defined as indication, explicitly not cause.
Log-normal distribution observation leads to interesting-feature task.

language_observations.summary: 'In TASK N:' labeled abstract structure mirroring section numbers.
'We have more than 80% confidence' empirical confidence claim.
Homer anecdote as non-standard hook for MCM paper.
'You may be wondering why' second-person reader engagement.
'In this paper, we try our best' effort-framing.
'By reviewing the literature, we learned' gap-identification.
'By analogy with the life cycle of online public opinion' lifecycle framing.
'Wordle has become a social currency' metaphor in letter.
'Thanks for taking time out of your busy schedule' formal closing.

judge_relevance_hypotheses.summary: Interpretable Gaussian+Poisson decomposition shows statistical rigor.
Popularity relaxation function is an original correction.
Bagging-integrated BP NN shows ensemble methodology awareness.
Explicit indication-not-cause caveat shows conceptual clarity.

weaknesses.summary: 8 word attributes all null on hard mode — weak attribute selection.
Sub-training set homogeneity risk from small dataset.
K=4 chosen by trial, no elbow method or silhouette.

independent_extensions.summary: Apply lifecycle period boundaries via changepoint detection instead of visual inspection.
Use silhouette score for optimal K selection in difficulty clustering.
Integrate social network analysis for comprehensive popularity prediction.
